record.title: Written on the Wall II, Graph Conjecture 103
record.statement: **WOWII Conjecture 103.** For every simple connected graph $G$, $a(G) \leq \left\lfloor b(G) - \ln\left(\frac{1}{|V(G)|}\sum_{v\in V(G)}\operatorname{ecc}(v)\right) \right\rfloor$, where $a(G)$ is the independence number and $b(G)$ is the order of a largest induced bipartite subgraph of $G$.
record.source_name: Open Math Problems Claimed to Be Solved with AI

record.title: Babai's problem
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with identity $1$, and let
$\operatorname{Irr}(G)$ denote the set of irreducible complex characters of $G$.
For a generating subset $S \subseteq G \setminus \{1\}$, let
$\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$ be the Cayley digraph with vertex set $G$ and arc set
$\{(g, sg) : g \in G,\ s \in S\}$; when $S = S^{-1}$ this digraph is identified
with the (undirected) Cayley graph of $G$ with respect to $S$. Two such digraphs
are isomorphic, written
$\operatorname{Cay}(G,S) \cong \operatorname{Cay}(G,S')$, if there is a
bijection of their vertex sets carrying arcs onto arcs. For a positive integer
$\nu$ put

$$
M_{\nu}^{S} = \left\{ \sum_{s \in S} \chi(s) \;\middle|\; \chi \in \operatorname{Irr}(G),\ \chi(1) = \nu \right\}.
$$

Then for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $\nu$, and all
generating subsets $S, S'$ of $G \setminus \{1\}$,

$$
\operatorname{Cay}(G,S) \cong \operatorname{Cay}(G,S') \implies M_{\nu}^{S} = M_{\nu}^{S'};
$$

that is,
$M_{\nu}^{S}$ depends only on the isomorphism type of the graph $\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$.

A finite group
$G$ for which this implication holds for all inverse-closed generating subsets $S,
T \subseteq G \setminus \{1\}$ and all positive integers $\nu$ is called a
BI-group; determine the finite groups that are BI-groups.
record.source_name: Wikipedia
record.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Babai's problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babai%27s_problem), the article this problem comes from.

record.title: Selfridge's conjecture
record.statement:
Call an odd natural number $k$ a Sierpi\'nski number if every member of the set

$$
\left\{\,k\cdot 2^{n}+1 : n\in\mathbb{N},\ n\ge 1\,\right\}
$$

is composite, i.e. $k\cdot 2^{n}+1$ is composite for all positive integers $n$.

Then
$78557$ is a Sierpi\'nski number, and it is the smallest one: for every odd integer $k$
with $1\le k<78557$ there exists a positive integer $n$ such that $k\cdot
2^{n}+1$ is prime.
record.source_name: Wikipedia
record.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Sierpiński number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierpi%C5%84ski_number), the article this problem comes from.

record.title: The cross-number equality conjecture for finite Abelian groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite Abelian group. For a sequence $S=(g_1,\ldots,g_l)$ over $G$, define its cross number by

$$
\mathsf{k}(S)=\sum_{i=1}^{l}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ord}(g_i)}.
$$

Let $\mathsf{k}(G)$ be the maximum of $\mathsf{k}(S)$ over zero-sumfree sequences $S$ over $G$, and let $\mathsf{K}(G)$ be the maximum over minimal zero-sum sequences. Let $\mathsf{k}^*(G)$ and $\mathsf{K}^*(G)$ denote the corresponding standard lower-bound expressions. **Cross-number equality conjecture.** For every finite Abelian group $G$,

$$
\mathsf{k}^*(G)=\mathsf{k}(G) \quad\text{and}\quad \mathsf{K}^*(G)=\mathsf{K}(G).
$$

These equalities are known for Abelian $p$-groups and some other special cases; no counterexample is known in general.
record.source_name: Benjamin Girard, “A new upper bound for the cross number of finite Abelian groups”, arXiv:0712.0331 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.0331

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2007).

record.title: The category conjecture for unordered Euclidean configuration spaces
record.statement:
Let $B(\mathbb R^n,k)$ be the unordered configuration space of $k$ points in Euclidean $n$-space, and let $\operatorname{cat}$ denote Lusternik–Schnirelmann category.

**Category conjecture.** For all $n$ and $k$,

$$
\operatorname{cat}(B(\mathbb R^n,k))=(k-1)\cdot(n-1).
$$

The paper presents this as a plausible analogue of the corresponding result for ordered configuration spaces. It would give a simple exact formula for the category of unordered Euclidean configuration spaces; the supplied source does not establish the claim or indicate a resolution.
record.source_name: Fridolin Roth, “On the category of Euclidean configuration spaces and associated fibrations”, arXiv:0904.1013 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.1013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2009).

record.title: Additivity conjecture for minimum output entropy of quantum channels
record.statement:
Let a quantum channel be a linear completely positive trace-preserving map $\Phi:\mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})\to\mathcal{M}_k(\mathbb{C})$. Its minimum output entropy is

$$
H_{\min}(\Phi)=\min_{\substack{\rho\in\mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C}),\ \rho\geqslant 0\\ \operatorname{Tr}\rho=1}}H(\Phi(\rho)),
$$

where $H(\rho)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$. **Additivity conjecture.** For all quantum channels $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$, one has

$$
H_{\min}(\Phi_1\otimes\Phi_2)=H_{\min}(\Phi_1)+H_{\min}(\Phi_2).
$$

This conjecture was disproved by Hastings, who exhibited a counterexample for the choice $\Phi_1=\overline{\Phi_2}$; consequently, the asserted additivity does not hold for all quantum channels.
record.source_name: Benoît Collins and Ion Nechita, “Gaussianization and eigenvalue statistics for random quantum channels (III)”, arXiv:0910.1768 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1768

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2009). “This conjecture was disproved by Hastings in as follows: There exists a counterexample to the conjecture for the choice $\Phi_1=\overline{\Phi_2}$.”

record.title: Basic open semialgebraic cone conjecture for graphs (9) and (11)
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{G}}$ denote the cone associated with a graph $\mathcal{G}$. A **basic open semialgebraic set** is an open semialgebraic set defined by finitely many strict polynomial inequalities. **Basic open semialgebraic cone conjecture.** The cones $\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{G}}$ corresponding to the graphs (9) and (11) are basic open semialgebraic sets. If true, this would show that these cones do not meet their algebraic boundaries and that the maximum likelihood estimate does not exist for one observation on the corresponding graphs, resolving the indicated cases in the table.
record.source_name: Caroline Uhler, “Geometry of maximum likelihood estimation in Gaussian graphical models”, arXiv:1012.2643 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2643

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2010).

record.title: Equality of generalized commuting probabilities determines central quotient order
record.statement:
Let $G_{1}$ and $G_{2}$ be finite groups, and let $Pr^{2n}(G)$ denote the generalized commuting probability of $G$ at level $2n$. Write $Z(G)$ for the center of $G$. **The conjecture.** If

$$
Pr^{2n}(G_{1})=Pr^{2n}(G_{2})
$$

for every $n\geq0$, then

$$
\left\vert G_{1}/Z(G_{1})\right\vert=\left\vert G_{2}/Z(G_{2})\right\vert.
$$

The claim is motivated by the known fact that equality of all generalized commuting probabilities forces the commutator subgroups to have the same order. It is refuted by the groups $G_{2}$ and $G_{3}=D_{8}\times D_{8}$, which provide a counterexample to the opposite direction of the related isoclinism conjecture.
record.source_name: Yonah Cherniavsky, Avraham Goldstein, Vadim E. Levit and Robert Shwartz, “Hultman Numbers and Generalized Commuting Probability in Finite Groups”, arXiv:1403.3868 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.3868

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2014). “The groups $G_{2}$ and $G_{3}=D_{8}\times D_{8}$ give a counterexample to the opposite direction of Conjecture .”

record.title: Joint symmetry conjecture for q,t-rectangle numbers
record.statement:
For $a,b\geq 0$, define the q,t-rectangle numbers

$$
S_{a,b}(q,t)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal{R}^{\mathrm{word}}(\mathrm{N}^a\mathrm{E}^b)}q^{\mathsf{area}^*_{b,-a}(w)}t^{\mathsf{area}^*_{b,-a}(\operatorname{sw}_{b,-a}^-(w))}.
$$

Here $\mathsf{area}^*_{b,-a}$ is the adjusted area statistic defined using the minimum of the $(b,-a)$-levels. **Joint symmetry conjecture.** For all $a,b$,

$$
S_{a,b}(q,t)=S_{a,b}(t,q).
$$

The conjecture is known when $a=b$, where a stronger identity was proved in the cited literature; the general rectangular case remains conjectural in the source.
record.source_name: Drew Armstrong, Nicholas A. Loehr and Gregory S. Warrington, “Sweep maps: A continuous family of sorting algorithms”, arXiv:1406.1196 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.1196

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The exact shortest-cycle conjecture for oriented 3-graphs
record.statement:
Let $f(n)$ denote the minimum possible length of the shortest cycle in a tournament on $n$ vertices. **Exact shortest-cycle conjecture.** For $n\ge 4$ and $n \equiv 0,3,4 \text{or }7\pmod{12}$, we have

$$
f(n)=\frac{1}{3}n(n-1).
$$

The preceding bounds show that this value is attainable by the construction in the paper and is a lower bound in the stated congruence classes; the conjecture asserts that the construction is best possible.
record.source_name: Imre Leader and Ta Sheng Tan, “Cycles in Oriented 3-graphs”, arXiv:1409.0972 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0972

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

record.title: The exact count of subdivisions of $K_4$
record.statement:
Let $\phi(n)$ denote the maximum number of $K_4$-subdivisions in a graph with $n$ vertices. **Exact-count conjecture.** For every $n$, 
$$
\phi(n)=\binom{n-1}{3}.
$$
 The theorem preceding this conjecture gives the lower bound $\frac{1}{32}n^3-\frac{1}{16}n^2$ and the upper bound $\binom{n-1}{3}$, so the conjecture asserts that the upper bound attained by wheel graphs is always sharp.
record.source_name: Tillmann Miltzow, Jens M. Schmidt and Mingji Xia, “Counting K_4-Subdivisions”, arXiv:1411.4819 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.4819

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).

record.title: Király–Nagy–Pálvölgyi–Visontai conjecture on weakly cross intersecting set pair systems
record.statement:
Let $A_1,A_2,\dots,A_m$ and $B_1,B_2,\dots,B_m$ be sets such that $|A_i|=k$ and $|B_i|=l$ for all $1\le i\le m$. Suppose that $A_i\cap B_i=\emptyset$ for all $1\le i\le m$, and that $A_i\cap B_j\neq\emptyset$ or $A_j\cap B_i\neq\emptyset$ for all distinct $i,j$. Such a system is called a **$(k,l)$-weakly cross intersecting set pair system**, and let $m_{max}(k,l)$ denote the largest $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ for which one exists.

**Király–Nagy–Pálvölgyi–Visontai conjecture.**

$$
m_{max}(k,l)\leq 2\binom{k+l}{k}.
$$

Tuza's upper bound and the cited construction show that the conjectured bound is asymptotically sharp up to a factor approaching $1$. The conjecture concerns the maximum size of weakly cross intersecting set pair systems.
record.source_name: Zoltán Lóránt Nagy and Balázs Patkós, “On the number of maximal intersecting k-uniform families and further applications of Tuza's set pair method”, arXiv:1501.00648 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00648

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: Systematic codes violating the Griesmer bound at distance $2^r+2$
record.statement:
A **systematic code** is a code containing the information symbols as specified coordinates. The **Griesmer bound** is the standard lower bound on the length of a code in terms of its dimension and minimum distance.

**Systematic-code Griesmer conjecture.** For every integer $r\geq 3$, there exists a systematic code with distance $2^r+2$ that does not satisfy the Griesmer bound.

The conjecture extends the paper's explicit counterexample showing that the Griesmer bound need not hold for systematic nonlinear codes. Its status is not specified in the source.
record.source_name: Emanuele Bellini, Eleonora Guerrini, Alessio Meneghetti and Massimiliano Sala, “On the Griesmer bound for nonlinear codes”, arXiv:1502.07379 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.07379

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2015).

record.title: Chromatic number conjecture for matching graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let ${\rm ex}(G,rK_2)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $rK_2$-free subgraph of $G$. The matching graph ${\rm KG}(G,rK_2)$ has vertices corresponding to the copies of $rK_2$ in $G$, with adjacency given by edge-disjointness. **Chromatic number conjecture.** For every connected graph $G$ and every positive integer $r$, one has

$$
\chi({\rm KG}(G,rK_2))=|E(G)|-{\rm ex}(G,rK_2).
$$

This conjecture proposes an exact formula for the chromatic number of matching graphs in terms of the extremal number of edges in an $rK_2$-free subgraph. The surrounding results establish the formula for several classes, including suitable complete bipartite graphs, but the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Meysam Alishahi and Hossein Hajiabolhassan, “On The Chromatic Number of Matching Graphs”, arXiv:1507.08456 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.08456

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: The clique-count conjecture for complete minor-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $\textup{cliques}(n,t)$ denote the maximum number of cliques in an $n$-vertex graph with no $K_t$-minor. **Clique-count conjecture.**

$$
\textup{cliques}(n,t)=2^{t-2}(n-t+3)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad t\leq 49.
$$

The bound is motivated by complete multipartite graphs, and computer search verifies it for $t\leq 49$; examples based on $K_{c\times 2}$ disprove the bound for sufficiently large $t$, including every $t\geq 62$.
record.source_name: David R. Wood, “Cliques in Graphs Excluding a Complete Graph Minor”, arXiv:1511.04655 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2015).

record.title: Finite-dimensional Frobenius algebra conjecture for multiplication-comultiplication axioms
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional vector space equipped with an associative multiplication $\mu$ and a coassociative comultiplication $\delta$. Suppose that $A$, $\mu$, and $\delta$ satisfy the equations given in string notation by equations (39) and (40).

**Finite-dimensional Frobenius algebra conjecture.** Then $A$ admits a unit for $\mu$ and a counit for $\delta$, and is, in fact, a Frobenius algebra.

The equations are among the multiplication-comultiplication axioms of a Frobenius algebra, and the preceding discussion identifies the existence of a unit or counit as the remaining issue. The question is whether finite dimensionality forces these structures; the source presents this as an open question after unsuccessful attempts to find a counterexample.
record.source_name: Gathoni Kamau-Devers, Gail Jardine and David Yetter, “A general state-sum construction of 2-dimensional topological quantum field theories with defects”, arXiv:1602.07999 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.07999

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

record.title: Positive gap above two-thirds for modularity of random cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,3}$ be a random cubic graph on $n$ vertices, and let $q^*(G_{n,3})$ denote its maximum modularity. **Positive-gap conjecture for random cubic graphs.** There exists a constant $\delta>0$ such that, with high probability as $n\to\infty$,

$$
q^*(G_{n,3})\geq \frac{2}{3}+\delta.
$$

This is the opposite of the possibility that the maximum modularity of a random cubic graph converges in probability to $2/3$; it would show that random cubic graphs have modularity uniformly bounded above two-thirds with high probability.
record.source_name: Colin McDiarmid and Fiona Skerman, “Modularity of regular and treelike graphs”, arXiv:1606.09101 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.09101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

record.title: The maximum stable-state count conjecture for neighborhood grids
record.statement: Let $P$ be a point configuration on $n^2$ points, and let $f^{(n,\ldots,n)}$ denote the number of standard Young tableaux of the square partition $(n,\ldots,n)$, equivalently the number of stable states of the identity configuration. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the conjecture concerns the number of stable states of arbitrary point configurations on these points. **Maximum stable-state count conjecture.** The number of stable states of any point configuration $P$ on $n^2$ points is less than or equal to $f^{(n,\ldots,n)}$. This would identify the identity configuration as attaining the maximum number of stable states among configurations with $n^2$ points; the source reports supporting results for $n\in\{1,2,3\}$ and computational experiments, but gives no resolution in general.
record.source_name: Martin Skrodzki, Ulrich Reitebuch and Alex McDonough, “Combinatorial and Asymptotical Results on the Neighborhood Grid”, arXiv:1710.03435 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.03435

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2017).

record.title: The depth bound conjecture for conflict-free connection colorings of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree. Let $D(T)$ be the minimum depth produced by Algorithm $1$ over all possible priorities for removing edges of $T$:

$$
D(T)=\min\{d(T)\mid d(T)\text{ is the depth of }T\text{ for a certain priority of removing edges of }T\text{ in Algorithm }1\}.
$$

Here $cfc(T)$ denotes the conflict-free connection number of $T$. **Depth bound conjecture.** For every tree $T$,

$$
D(T)<2cfc(T).
$$

The conjecture would show that the algorithmic depth bound is always within a factor of two of the optimum conflict-free connection number. The paper notes examples with $k<D(A_k)<2k$ and establishes the algorithm's correctness, but does not state a general proof of this strict inequality.
record.source_name: Hong Chang, Meng Ji, Xueliang Li and Jingshu Zhang, “Conflict-free connection of trees”, arXiv:1712.10010 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.10010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: The conjectured formula for the first minimum zero eigenvalue multiplicity
record.statement:
Let $m_1^0(n,w)$ denote the minimum multiplicity of the first zero eigenvalue in the relevant Johnson-scheme setting, with parameters $n$ and $w$. The preceding results reduce its determination to comparing explicit candidate values, and computational evidence motivates the following claim.

**Conjectured identity.** For $w\geq 5$ and $n\geq 2w+1$,

$$
m_1^0(n,w)=2{n-2 \choose w-1}.
$$

The identity is supported by computations for $6\leq n\leq 600$ and $3\leq w\leq n/2$; the paper presents it as a conjecture, so its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: I. Yu. Mogilnykh, K. V. Vorob'ev and A. A. Valyuzhenich, “MMS-type problems for Johnson scheme”, arXiv:1810.04075 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04075

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2018). “The real behaviour of the growth rate of $m_2^{-}(n,3)$ remains to be an intriguing open problem.”

record.title: Dimension conjecture for dual cells
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a dual $k$-cell, and let its affine span be the smallest affine subspace containing $D$.

**Dimension conjecture.** For every dual $k$-cell, the dimension of its affine span is equal to $k$.

The conjecture is known for $k\leq 3$ because all dual $3$-cells are classified. A counterexample would immediately give a counterexample to the Voronoi conjecture, while the assertion remains open in higher dimensions.
record.source_name: Alexey Garber, “Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional parallelohedra”, arXiv:1906.05193 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2019). “The Voronoi conjecture is proved in small dimensions $d\leq 4$.”

record.title: Muffin problem one-third lower-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $f(m,s)$ be the largest possible size of the smallest assigned muffin piece, where $m$ is the number of muffins and $s$ the number of students.

**One-third lower-bound conjecture.** For all $m>s\geq 2$,

$$
f(m,s)\geq 1/3.
$$

The conjecture is solved: the paper states that Cui et al. (2018) proved it, and gives a simpler proof.
record.source_name: Richard E. Chatwin, “An Optimal Solution for the Muffin Problem”, arXiv:1907.08726 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.08726

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2019). “The second conjecture has been proved by Cui et al. (2018) (see Theorem 20 therein).”

record.title: Asplund–Fox extension conjecture for corona coprime numbers
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, let $\overline{K}_m$ be the edgeless graph on $m$ vertices, and let $\mathfrak{pr}(G)$ denote the minimum coprime number of a graph $G$. **Asplund–Fox's corona conjecture.** For all positive integers $m$, there exists an $M>m$ such that for all $n>M$, 
$$
\mathfrak{pr}(K_n\odot\overline{K}_m)=p_{n-1},
$$
 where $p_{n-1}$ is the $(n-1)$st prime number. The paper's theorem proves the stronger exact formula $\mathfrak{pr}(K_n\odot\overline{K}_m)=\max(mn+n,p_{n-1})$ for all positive integers $m,n$, so this conjecture is solved.
record.source_name: Catherine Lee, “Minimum coprime graph labelings”, arXiv:1907.12670 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.12670

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Uniform deficit conjecture for 1-cross intersecting set pair systems
record.statement:
Let $m_n(*, *, 1)$ denote the maximum size of a $(1,1,1)$-? set pair system on an $n$-element ground set under the notation of the paper. **Uniform deficit conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $\varepsilon$ such that

$$
m_n(*, *, 1)\le(1-\varepsilon){2n\choose n}
$$

for every $n\ge 2$. This predicts a uniform positive gap below the central binomial coefficient for these systems; the source presents it as a belief, and no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Zoltán Füredi, András Gyárfás and Zoltán Király, “Problems and results on 1-cross intersecting set pair systems”, arXiv:1911.03067 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03067

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

record.title: The bounded-difference conjecture for maximum-coefficient locations
record.statement: For odd $n\geq 35$, let $D_n$ be the half-difference between the two locations of the maximum absolute coefficients of $(q;q)_n$, and define $E_n=D_n-D_{n-4}$. **Bounded-difference conjecture.** For all odd $n\geq 35$, $E_n\in\{0,1,2\}$, and $E_n>0$ for all odd $n\geq 61$. The claim is supported in the source by explicit computations for $n\leq 75000$, but no proof is given.
record.source_name: Alexander Berkovich and Ali K. Uncu, “Where do the maximum absolute q-series coefficients of (1-q)(1-q^2)(1-q^3)(1-q^n-1)(1-q^n) occur?”, arXiv:1911.03707 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.03707

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2019).

record.title: The induced-subgraph degree conjecture for Cayley graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $S$ be a symmetric set of non-identity elements generating $G$. Let $X=(G,S)$ be the corresponding undirected Cayley graph, and for $U\subseteq G$ let $X(U)$ denote the induced subgraph of $X$ on $U$. **The induced-subgraph degree conjecture.** For every $U\subseteq G$ satisfying

$$
|U|>\frac{|G|}{2},
$$

the maximum degree of $X(U)$ is at least

$$
\sqrt{|S|/2}.
$$

Huang proved the analogous statement for the Boolean cube, and Alon and Zheng proved it for Cayley graphs of $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$. The paper proves the conjecture for Cayley graphs of finite abelian groups; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Aaron Potechin and Hing Yin Tsang, “A Conjecture on Induced Subgraphs of Cayley Graphs”, arXiv:2003.13166 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.13166

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

record.title: The periodic-point conjecture for the stack-sorting maps $s_{\{132,213\}}$ and $s_{\{231,213\}}$
record.statement: Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of length $n$, and let $s_{\{132,213\}}$ and $s_{\{231,213\}}$ be the corresponding stack-sorting maps. A permutation is **periodic** if some positive iterate of the relevant map sends it back to itself. **Periodic-point conjecture.** The only periodic points of $s_{\{132,213\}}$ and $s_{\{231,213\}}$ are the identity permutation and its reverse. This conjecture concerns the eventual periodic behavior of these restricted stack-sorting maps; the preceding results determine periodic points for related maps, while the asserted classification for these two maps remains unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Katalin Berlow, “Restricted Stacks as Functions”, arXiv:2008.01164 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01164

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

record.title: The star spanning tree minimum intersection conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph that admits a **star spanning tree** $T_s$. Let $\mathscr{T}_G$ denote the set of spanning trees of $G$, and let $\cap(T)$ be the intersection number of a spanning tree $T$. **Star spanning tree minimum intersection conjecture.** For every spanning tree $T\in\mathscr{T}_G$,

$$
\cap(T_s)\leq\cap(T).
$$

This conjecture generalizes the corresponding result for complete graphs and asserts that a star spanning tree minimizes the intersection number among all spanning trees of any graph admitting one. The surrounding discussion describes reductions that would apply to a hypothetical counterexample, but provides no resolution of the conjecture.
record.source_name: Manuel Dubinsky, César Massri and Gabriel Taubin, “Minimum Spanning Tree Cycle Intersection Problem”, arXiv:2102.13193 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.13193

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: The commutator-width conjecture for traces in \(\Gamma(2)'\)
record.statement: Let $\Gamma(2)'$ be the commutator subgroup of $\Gamma(2)$, and let $\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma(2)')$ denote its trace set. The **commutator width** of an element is the minimum number of commutators needed to express it. **The commutator-width conjecture.** For every $t\in\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma(2)')$, there exists $\gamma\in\Gamma(2)'$ such that $\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma)=t$ and $\gamma$ has commutator width either 1 or 2. Computational results in the paper show that some traces have no 1-commutator representative, motivating the asserted bound of 2; the general statement remains open.

record.title: Discrete geometry and automorphic forms (problem 9)
record.statement: Let $A_-(d)$ be the minimum or $r$ for which there exists a Schwartz function $f \colon \mathbb R^d \to \mathbb R$ such that $f(0) = \hat f(0) = 1$, $f(x) \leq 0$ for $|x| \geq r$, and $\hat f(y) \geq 0$ for all $y$. For $d$ a non-integral positive number this bound is still defined by using radial functions and the Bessel transform. We know $A_-(1) = 1$, $A_-(8) = \sqrt{2}$, and $A_-(24) = 2$. Numerically it seems to be the case that $A_-(2) = (4/3)^{1/4}$, and that $A_-'(8) = \sqrt{2}/30 = (\sqrt(2))^7/240$ and $A_-'(24) = 368/12285 = 23 * 2^8/196560$.

record.title: Conjecture 5.24 — (Picard number one conjecture for level L structures).
record.statement: (Picard number one conjecture for level L structures). Prove that H2(Modg[L]; Q) = Q when g≥ 3. More generally, compute H2(Modg[L]; Z) for all g≥ 3,L≥ 2. Harer [ Har2] proved this conjecture in the case L = 1. This generalization was stated (for Picard groups) as Question 7.12 in [ HL]. The case L = 2 was claimed in [ F o], but there is apparently an error in the proof. At this point even the ( g,L ) = (3, 2) case is open. Here is a possible approach to Conjecture 5.24 for g≥ 4. First note that, since Mod g[L] is a finite index subgroup of the finitely presented group Mod g, it is finitely presented. As we have a lot of explicit information about the finite group Sp(2 g, Z/LZ), it seems possible in principle to answer the following, which is also a test of our understanding of Mod g[L].

record.title: Question 7.4 — Is there a unique (up to conjugacy) minimal dilation pseudo-Anosov in Modg?
record.statement: Is there a unique (up to conjugacy) minimal dilation pseudo-Anosov in Modg? Note that this is true for g = 1; the unique minimum is realized by the conjugacy class of the matrix ( 2 1 1 1 ). Here is a natural refinement of the problem of finding L(Modg). Fix a genus g. Fix a possible r-tuple ( k1,...,k r) of singularity data for Σ g. By this we mean to consider possible foliations withr singularities with k1,...,k r prongs, respectively. For a fixed g, there are only finitely many possible tuples, as governed by the Poincare-Hopf index theorem. Masur-Smillie [ MS] proved that, for every admissible tuple, there is some pseudo-Anosov on Σ g with stable foliation having the given singularity data. Hence the following makes sense. 2. record.title: Possible “fake CM” forcing even rank
record.statement:
The elliptic curve of discriminant $-114$ given by
$$E:
 y^2=x^3+\frac{5}{4}x^2-2x-7$$
has everywhere good reduction over $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[12]{-11})$. Its global root number is $+1$ over every finite extension of $K$, so its rank should be even over any number field containing $\sqrt[12]{-11}$. This elliptic curve does not have complex multiplication, which could in principle account for this behaviour of the rank. Is it nevertheless possible to find some extra structure (“fake CM”) on $E$ that forces the rank to be always even?

record.title: Greuel–Lossen–Shustin conjecture for linear systems associated with plane-curve singularities
record.statement:
Let $S_1,\\ldots,S_r$ be equisingular singularity types, and let $m_1,m_2,m_3$ be the three largest multiplicities occurring in their associated multiplicity sequences. Define
\[
C(S_1,\ldots,S_r)=\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}\binom{\operatorname{mult}_{p_{ij}}S_i+1}{2}.
\]
For a composition of point blowups $\pi:X\to\mathbb P^2$ that is general among those whose centers $p_{11},\ldots,p_{1k_1},\ldots,p_{r1},\ldots,p_{rk_r}$ satisfy the proximities dictated by $S_1,\ldots,S_r$, and for every $d\ge m_1+m_2+m_3$, is it true that
\[
\dim\left|d\pi^*L-\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}(\operatorname{mult}_{p_{ij}}S_i)E_{ij}\right|
=\max\left\{-1,\binom{d+2}{2}-C(S_1,\ldots,S_r)-1\right\}?
\]

record.title: Strong Lehmer conjecture for the height of algebraic numbers
record.statement:
Let $h$ denote the absolute logarithmic Weil height on a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$. Northcott’s theorem implies that there is a function $C:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that, for every $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $\alpha\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ with $\deg(\alpha)\le d$, one has $h(\alpha)\ge C(d)$ or $h(\alpha)=0$. The strong version of the Lehmer conjecture stated in the report predicts that
\[
C(d)=\frac{\log \ell}{d},
\]
where $\ell=1.176280\ldots$ is the largest real root of $x^{10}+x^9-x^7-x^6-x^5-x^4-x^3+x+1$.

record.title: Purely inseparable extensions of valued fields in mixed characteristic
record.statement:
Question 10 (posed by Franz-Viktor Kuhlmann): “What are the purely inseparable extensions of a valued field in mixed characteristic?” In characteristic $(p,p)$:

$K$ is henselian defectless $(n=e\cdot f)$ if and only if $K$ is algebraically maximal (no immediate algebraic extensions) and every finite purely inseparable extension is defectless.

In characteristic $(0,p)$:

$K$ is henselian defectless if and only if $K$ is algebraically maximal and [find a nice simple criterion for the missing condition].

record.title: Maximum number of almost-similar triangles for almost regular targets
record.statement: Let $T$ be a triangle whose angles all lie between $59^\circ$ and $61^\circ$. For a fixed $\varepsilon>0$, call a triangle $\varepsilon$-similar to $T$ if, after matching the angles, each corresponding angle differs by less than $\varepsilon$. Let $h(n,T,\varepsilon)$ be the maximum number of such triangles determined by an $n$-point set in the plane. Then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every positive integer $n$, $$h(n,T,\varepsilon)\leq \frac{1}{24}(n^3-n).$$ In particular, when $n$ is a power of $3$, $$h(n,T,\varepsilon)=\frac{1}{24}(n^3-n).$$

record.title: A superlinear lower bound on the number of 5-holes
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane in general position, meaning that no three points of $P$ are collinear. A set $H$ of $k$ points from $P$ is a $k$-hole in $P$ if $H$ is the vertex set of a convex polygon containing no other points of $P$. For positive integers $n$ and $k$, let $h_k(n)$ be the minimum number of $k$-holes in a set of $n$ points in general position in the plane. Then there is a fixed constant $c>0$ such that, for every integer $n\ge 10$, $h_5(n)\ge c n\log^{4/5} n$.

record.title: Bounds for sums of a prime and $k$-th powers
record.statement:
Let $H(k)$ be the smallest number $s$ such that every sufficiently large natural number is the sum of a prime and $s$ natural $k$-th powers. Let $c_r$, for $r=4$ or $5$, be the unique solution in $[1,\binfty)$ of

$$2c_r=2+\blog(rc_r-1).$$

Then

$$H(k)\ble c_5k+4.$$

If the Riemann hypothesis holds for all Dirichlet $L$-functions, then

$$H(k)\ble c_4k+4.$$

Here $c_5=2.134693\ldots$ and $c_4=1.961969\ldots$.

record.title: The Dynamic Optimality Conjecture for Splay Trees
record.statement:
Prove that there is a universal constant C such that, for every access sequence, the cost of the splay-tree algorithm is at most C times the minimum cost of any offline dynamic binary search tree algorithm, up to the standard additive initialization term.

Source: [Petr Chmel et al., Splay trees are almost dynamically optimal (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18498).
